response.title: Does a pellet stove need a special kind of battery backup, or will any power station or computer battery backup work?
response.answer:
A pellet stove does not necessarily need a special battery backup, but not every power station or computer UPS will work properly.

The most important factors are the output waveform, power capacity, and switchover time.

A good battery backup for a pellet stove should have:

Pure sine wave output — Important for the stove's combustion blower, convection fan, auger motor, and electronics. Modified sine wave inverters can cause motor noise, overheating, or unreliable operation.

Enough continuous and surge power — Pellet stoves often consume roughly 80–300 watts while running, but the electric igniter can temporarily push consumption to 300–600 watts or more, depending on the model.

Fast automatic switchover — If you want the stove to keep running when utility power fails, the backup needs to take over quickly enough that the stove's control board doesn't reset.

Enough battery capacity — This determines whether the stove can operate for minutes or hours.

Comparing your options

Yes, if compatible

Pellet stove-specific UPS

Designed for stove operation, but check model compatibility




Basic modified sine wave inverter

	

Not recommended

How long will a power station last?

For example, assuming the pellet stove averages 150 watts while running and accounting for approximately 85% usable AC energy:

Actual runtime depends on the stove's electrical consumption, inverter losses, and ignition cycles.

One important exception: manufacturer-specific behavior

Some pellet stoves are designed to recognize a UPS and automatically enter a safe shutdown mode rather than continue heating. For example, certain Harman models have specific approved UPS devices and operating settings. 
Pellet Stove Parts 4 Less
+1

ComfortBilt, by contrast, explicitly allows compatible pure sine wave UPS units, power stations, and inverters, subject to its power requirements. 
SMG HEARTH & HOME LLC

My recommendation: If you want the stove to keep heating during an outage, look for a pure sine wave power station with UPS functionality and roughly 1,000 Wh or more of battery capacity, provided your stove manufacturer approves it. If you only want enough time for a safe shutdown, a compatible computer UPS may be sufficient.

Two questions:

What brand and model is your pellet stove? (Harman, Quadra-Fire, ComfortBilt, Englander, etc.)

Do you want it to keep heating during a power outage, or just shut down safely?

With those details, I can tell you whether a regular computer UPS or an EcoFlow/Jackery-style power station will work, and what specifications you actually need.
